searchText: As 7623 implements it, 99% of the txs remain unaffected. What we really prevent is the worst cases where compressed max EL payload size is 27x the average. 7623 wouldn't really change the median/average block size but more diffuses worst cases. With 9 blobs we'd be at 1.125 MiB max, 0.375 more than today. EIP-7623 can limit the worst case EL payload size by 0.72 MiB. With the recent community push to increase the gas limit, I am very much in favor of implementing 7623 yesterday not in the future. We might face large block issues similar to what happened on sepolia previously which is not pleasant. Additionally, we agreed to drop premerge history on may 1st, but if gas limit is raised without this eip, we will definitely need to do it way earlier which will put a lot of pressure on execution client devs given pectra's workload as well. Btw - is someone working here on an EIP pricings to make the precompile not bad? I am thinking fusaka would be a good scope for that anyway - as per our discussion at bangkok: https://github.com/ethereum/EIPs/pull/9049 this limits the gas limit to transactions by 30 millions This would also help with worst case for parallel evm implementations yeah - mostly this deals with quadratic cases, now they do not grow indefinetely :) I actually would put this and 7623 (they are very easy) and then increase gas limit my feel from bangkok is that - most issues are addressed with these 2 Btw - is someone working here on an EIP Paired with a block gas increase 7623 would make sense. In isolation it is a net negative IMHO. in isolation it is not a net negative because the 3.5 MB block is an attack you would still reduce the net negative - no reason why a malicious block should be allowed at all average block is 75kb - spike is around 200ish kbs. 3.5 MB is clearly a well-crafted outlier In a Proof of Work world propagating a 3.5MB concerns me as it could be used to advance one of the variours chain split attacks, but in a Proof of Stake world what validator is going to waste their slot on a bad block? Not to mention the multipe that would be needed? It's all downside for the proposer. Maybe if a block builder goes rogue but that would be the end of their buisniess. Simply increasing a cost with no way to absorb it elsewhere will result in lower TPS, unless we can expect a change in the character of transactions as a result.
